dict.string: Configure FirstRun, the Jamf Pro device-assignment app for iPhone, iPad, and Apple TV. A technician assigns the device to a site (Jamf Pro building) and, optionally, a role; FirstRun writes the assignment back to the device's Jamf Pro record.
The human-readable description of this payload. This description appears on the Detail screen.
The human-readable name for the profile payload. The name appears on the Detail screen and doesn't need to be unique.

The reverse-DNS-style identifier for the payload. This identifier is usually the same as the TopLevel value, with an additional appended component. This string must be unique within the profile. During a profile replacement, the system updates payloads with the same 'PayloadIdentifier' and 'PayloadUUID' in the old and new profiles.
The payload type, which each payload domain's reference page specifies.

The globally unique identifier for the payload. The actual content is unimportant, but must be globally unique. In macOS, use 'uuidgen' to generate UUIDs. During a profile replacement, the system updates payloads with the same 'PayloadIdentifier' and 'PayloadUUID' in the old and new profiles.
The version of this specific payload.
The human-readable string containing the name of the organization that provides the profile. This value doesn't need to match the organization payload value in the enclosing dictionary.

Base URL of the Jamf Pro tenant FirstRun talks to, including the scheme.
Enter the tenant root only — no trailing slash and no '/api' path — FirstRun appends its own endpoints (/api/oauth/token, /api/v1/buildings, /JSSResource/mobiledevices/…).
Example: https://your-tenant.jamfcloud.com
If this key is missing, empty, or not a parsable URL, FirstRun shows its "Configuration Required" screen instead of the onboarding flow.

Client ID of the Jamf Pro API client used for the OAuth client-credentials grant (Jamf Pro → Settings → System → API roles and clients).
The associated API role needs, at minimum: Read Mobile Devices, Update Mobile Devices, and Read Buildings — plus read/write on any extension attributes named below.

Managed App Configuration supports OAuth client credentials only. The username and password (basic auth) option in the app is available exclusively through the on-device manual configuration editor, and cannot be delivered by MDM.
Client secret paired with the OAuth Client ID above. FirstRun exchanges it for a short-lived access token that is cached in memory only and never written to disk.

This value is a credential. Deliver it in an encrypted profile or through your MDM's App Configuration, never in a plain-text profile committed to source control, and rotate it if it is ever exported in the clear.

Serial number of the device being set up. It must match the device's record in Jamf Pro inventory — FirstRun looks the device up by serial and refuses to submit if the lookup does not match.
Leave this as the Jamf Pro variable $SERIALNUMBER so the serial is substituted at install time, or type a literal serial for a single-device test deployment.

FirstRun treats any value that still begins with '$' as an unsubstituted variable and refuses to start. If devices land on the "Configuration Required" screen with a literal $SERIALNUMBER, the MDM is not performing variable substitution — check that the value is delivered as App Configuration rather than pasted into a static payload.

Roles offered on the Role step, shown in the order listed here.
Leave this list empty (or omit the key) to skip the Role step entirely — the technician then goes straight from picking a site to submitting.

Optional helper text shown beneath a role once the technician selects it.
Each entry's key is the role name as it appears in Setup Role Options; the value is the description. Matching ignores letter case and surrounding whitespace. Roles with no entry — or with an empty description — simply show no helper text.
Entries whose key does not correspond to a role in Setup Role Options are ignored. They are harmless, but they will never be displayed.
The role name, exactly as listed in Setup Role Options.
The description shown under that role when it is selected.
Shared check-in and scheduling device at the front desk.

Display name of the mobile device extension attribute in Jamf Pro that receives the selected role when the technician submits.
The name must match the extension attribute in Jamf Pro exactly. Leave this unset to collect the role in the flow without writing it to inventory.
Nothing is written unless a role is actually chosen, so this key has no effect while Setup Role Options is empty.

Display name of the mobile device extension attribute that receives an ISO 8601 timestamp of the moment the role was submitted (for example 2026-09-03T14:22:31Z).
Written only when Setup Role Extension Attribute is also set and a role was chosen.
